- OIML R 76-1:2006 for accuracy class (III) or (IIII) — these are accuracy class markings in oval shapes. I should transcribe them as ㏒ or as text. They're the classic oval class marks: (III) and (IIII). I'll transcribe as ⑶ ... Let me use (III) or (IIII) — perhaps with the oval notation like ⬭. Best to write them as (III) or (IIII) with a note that they're in oval shapes? The rules say don't annotate. I'll transcribe as the class marks. The images show ovals containing "III" and "IIII". I'll represent them as ㏒... no. Simply: OIML R 76-1:2006 for accuracy class (III) or (IIII). Perhaps I could use the Unicode characters Ⓘ? There's no perfect oval. I'll just use (III) or (IIII).

Actually, the accuracy class marks are typically shown as an ellipse with Roman numerals. To transcribe them, I could write them as "⑂"... no. Just plain text (III) and (IIII) is fine.

- This Certificate relates only to the metrological and technical characteristics of the type of measuring instrument covered by the relevant OIML International Recommendation above-identified. This Certificate does not bestow any form of legal international approval.
